background: Bank of Ireland Group is the holding company of Ireland's other dominant retail and business bank, funded by Irish deposits and lending on Irish and UK mortgages and to Irish companies, with a UK consumer finance arm.
synthesis: The group is rated A- on average across two of the three main agencies, both on a stable outlook; the third withdrew its rating on 25 Mar 2026. Capital is mixed against EU and Nordic peers: CET1 of 14.9% is below the peer median, but leverage of 6.8% is in the top quarter. Liquidity is a clear strength, with LCR of 193% and NSFR of 153% both in the top quarter. Leverage has risen 0.5 points since 30 Jun 2024 and the rest has been flat, and everything flagged in the last 90 days is good news on profit, including the first-half result reported on 1 Aug 2026.
